texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Thanks for joining this journey so willingly.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: So... I suppose you want to ask, "Where are we?" It's a difficult place to put a name to. It belongs to the concept of the sixth floor, but it's also where all the floors you've passed through flow backward, mixing and grinding together into sediment.
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Unsold inventory, out-of-season stock, carryovers, returns, and things passed over until even the store forgot they were there. Those distinctions mean nothing here, because everything you've gone through so far has been crushed and mixed up in the same heap beneath your feet.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Layer pressed upon layer... until they all became this hard, slippery hill.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Try not to give too much thought, whatever you happen to tread on.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>Your task is simple, Meursault. Push the boulder all the way to the top.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>There's no trick to it. Just apply some force, hold your course, and keep pushing.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>Some stretches may be too slippery. Others may be too steep.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: But you can do it, Meursault. Remember all that training I put you through?
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>Well, would you look at that.</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>Models. Walking the runway.</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>They walk to the end, turn around... and walk back. Right where they started. Around they turn, and off they go again.</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>Hah! Ring any bells? Looks rather like what you're doing, doesn't it?</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>How are your arms holding up, by the way? I'd love to make you some tea... but perhaps not. You'd have to let go of that boulder to hold the teacup, after all.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>Starting for the first time and returning to the starting point are entirely different things, Meursault.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>First times are always the same—you have nothing to lose because you're oblivious to what's involved. But the second time starting over, and then the next... You know how far up you need to push the boulder again.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>Pfft... Oops, I wasn't laughing at you!</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>Or maybe you expected me to offer you some sort of platitude?</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>Here's what I think, actually. Sometimes, failure is just failure. Not every defeat comes with a lesson to be learned.</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#7d7d7d>Does it anger you? That is what a prison is for.</color>
texts.speaker: The Chaplain

texts.text: <color=#7d7d7d>To keep pushing, knowing it will roll back down... To believe that this time you will reach the end, only to have that certainty shattered to pieces. That is your punishment.</color>
texts.speaker: The Chaplain

texts.text: <color=#7d7d7d>This is the path of penance. A road of suffering... laid to punish you, O Sinful One.</color>
texts.speaker: The Chaplain

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Models don't stop once the runway show begins.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>I wonder if that's what makes their walk beautiful.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Or is it the other way around? Do they keep walking because they have to look beautiful?</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>To become a model was the dream of everyone living in Grand Magasin Sisyphe.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>It's a dream realized only by wearing expensive clothes and being the subject of countless gazes. That is why everyone was so desperate to climb even one floor higher.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>And yet, after climbing and climbing...</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>There's nothing left to do but to keep walking on the runway. What a thing to congratulate, hmm?</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>Say, have you ever wondered...</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: ... whether you're pushing the boulder, or if the boulder is pulling you uphill?
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>A fun little thought exercise, isn't it? Try letting go for a moment. I'm dying to see what happens.</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>Look straight ahead, Meursault.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>Keep that chin up. Feet flat against the ground.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>Don't let them see your suffering and nail it in their head as suffering.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#7d7d7d>This... is the punishment bestowed upon you, O Sinful One.</color>
texts.speaker: The Chaplain

texts.text: <color=#7d7d7d>Do not dare wish for it to end.</color>
texts.speaker: The Chaplain

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>The dregs of every floor you've passed through are mixed together here.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Look closely. You'll find whole heaps of eyeballs embedded in it.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Some have spent their entire lives collecting those.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>There must be tapes of my voice somewhere there, too.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>Every day, I went to work and read them that manual, word for word, top of the sheet to the bottom.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>That was my role. Whether I agreed with the words was irrelevant. The longings of the Grand Magasin's denizens, their pain, their delight... all of it was raw material for Canned Experiences.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>Shall I tell you how much farther to the top?</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>You want to know, don't you? It's eating you alive, isn't it?</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>You might be past the halfway point. Or... Hey, maybe you're just a few steps from the summit? Or, if not... Pfft! Perhaps you've barely left the starting line? Who knows?</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>It's all right to stop.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>Oh, you can't stop now!</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#7d7d7d>To bear the weight in full and do nothing but ascend. That is the lot of a sinner.</color>
texts.speaker: The Chaplain

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>The summit isn't what matters, Meursault. The important thing is...</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>People like to judge the journey by where it gets you.</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>Then again... we eat, only to grow hungry again.</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>We wash up, and become dirty again.</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>We sleep only to grow tired again. Each of us knows this is the truth. And yet...</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>We continue to prepare dinner, warm the bathwater, and turn out the light, saying "sleep tight"s and "good night"s.</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>Why do you force yourself to climb this hill, Meur?</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>You could have wrapped yourself in those chains and found peace of your own.</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>You've finally reached it. The top of the hill.</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>You can let go now.</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>The boulder will roll back down. But... that isn't what matters, is it?</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: Now come and see that child. Come see the Grand Magasin... Come see me.
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>The boulder will roll back down, but that's all right.</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#e1b643>Come see me now.</color>
texts.speaker: Carmen

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Come see me now.</color>
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <color=#7d7d7d>Come see me now.</color>
texts.speaker: The Chaplain

texts.text: <color=#ffe066>Come see me now.</color>
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>Come see me now.</color>
texts.speaker: Mother

texts.text:
You should be allowed to be who you are.
Not bound by anyone or anything.
There is a river that flows at the very bottom of the world.

As beings born as humans, we can't help but be affected by the dream of humanity that the river shares.
I won't deny that. It's just part of being human.
But "culture," which is acquired and unnatural, things that are determined by others... shouldn't define the shape.
I want you to be wholly yourself, even for a moment. In fact, I want mankind itself to be able to experience that.
I want to provide that opportunity, to grant the strength to achieve that.
After years upon years of toil and reflection, my junior's reached a certain enlightenment—and his philosophy was eventually set in a way that diverges from mine.
Ayin has the values I used to believe in and sought to convey to the world, and now seeks to give people... "tools." Clothes.
But my answer remains the same.

"You" must be allowed to remain wholly yourself.
Unshackled by anything.
